newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market inactive - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were typically quiet early Monday, with no reported sales or bids, feedlot sources said.

Cattle owners were asking $69.00 to $70.00 per cwt, with bids expected at $67.00 once they do surface, some sources said. Sales last week were active at $68.00, with most showlists sold out and some cattle pulled ahead.

Several feedlot managers said they expected cattle this week to sell at $68.00, steady with last week. Fed cattle prices were seen underpinned by projections for continued firm beef demand, they said.

Beef demand was expected to be fueled by retail buying for mid-month features and promotions for the Memorial Day holiday weekend later this month and the Fathers Day weekend in June, market sources said.
Beef prices last week were higher amid strong demand, with heavyweight choice Friday quoted up $0.55 at $106.23 per cwt, up $1.61 for the week, USDA statistics showed.

Fed cattle prices also were seen buoyed by ideas showlists will be steady to smaller than last week. Packer cattle buying was so active last week that several feedlots reported pulling cattle ahead from this week's showlists to meet the demand.
